newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico's Alestra says leads Monterrey ballot drive.
newsitem.headline: Mexico's Alestra says leads Monterrey ballot drive.

text.p: Mexican telephone firm Alestra, backed by U.S. long-distance giant AT&T Corp said it received 43 percent of pre-subscription ballots in its favor up to Jan. 10 in the northern city of Monterrey.
In a statement, it said the information came from NCSI International, which is monitoring the balloting process.

Monterrey, Mexico's third largest city, was the second industrial center to be opened to telephone competition this year. The first was Queretaro, in central Mexico, where Alestra also won most pre-subscription ballots.
The balloting process allows residents or businesses to select a long-distance carrier a month or two before their city opens to competition.
